key_insight: A 190 mm spray distance produced the most compact Cr3C2–NiCr coating and the best corrosion resistance on DSS 2205 in 1 M H2SO4.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing detonation-gun spray distance is a practical lever for improving coating integrity and extending the service life of stainless steel components in acidic industrial environments.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm.
Evaluated corrosion behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and potentiodynamic polarization.
Compared surface morphology and porosity by SEM to link microstructure with performance.
evidence_signal: Porosity dropped from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating showed the lowest corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy) versus 2.60 mmpy for uncoated DSS 2205.
watch_item: The optimum distance was established under one electrolyte, room temperature, and a limited set of spray distances, so broader operating conditions may shift the best setting.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
